content.user_title: Design Reliable Zapier and Make Automations
content.value_statement: No-code automations often fail because platform limits, bad data, and missing error handling are overlooked. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code plan reliable Zapier and Make workflows.
actual_capabilities: Compares Zapier and Make for workflow complexity, integrations, branching, and budget needs.
Explains basic trigger-action, sequential, and conditional branching automation patterns.
Identifies common Zapier and Make anti-patterns, including typed dropdown values and hardcoded fields.
Highlights reliability concerns such as error handling, duplicates, operation counting, and app updates.
Supports decisions about when an automation should move from no-code tools to coded services.
limitations: Does not connect to Zapier, Make, or third-party apps directly.
Does not validate live account permissions, pricing, app limits, or current integration availability.
Does not provide executable automation exports or platform-specific scenario files.
Requires the user to supply workflow requirements, data fields, and business rules.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Automation
use_cases.description: Choose Zapier or Make and outline triggers, actions, branches, and failure paths before building.

use_cases.title: Debug a Broken Workflow
use_cases.description: Review a failing Zap or scenario for dropdown misuse, missing error handling, duplicates, or app update changes.

use_cases.title: Assess No-Code Fit
use_cases.description: Decide whether a workflow should stay in no-code tools or move to an API-backed custom service.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Platform
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to automate this process: [describe process]. Compare Zapier and Make for this workflow and recommend one option.

prompt_templates.title: Map a Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Zapier or Make automation for [business process]. Include triggers, actions, branches, data fields, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Find Reliability Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this automation plan for failure risks: [paste plan]. Identify anti-patterns, duplicate risks, hardcoded values, and monitoring gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Decide When to Use Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate whether this automation should stay in Zapier or Make or move to custom code: [describe volume, logic, data, and integrations].

output_examples.input: A sales lead form should create a CRM contact, alert Slack, and assign a follow-up owner.
output_examples.output: Recommended platform: Zapier for a simple trigger-action workflow. Add duplicate checks, owner fallback rules, and an error notification step.

output_examples.input: A monthly invoice workflow needs branching by region, currency conversion, and exception review.
output_examples.output: Recommended platform: Make because the workflow needs branching and data transformation. Include an exception route and operation cost estimate.

output_examples.input: A support workflow breaks when a helpdesk app changes a field name.
output_examples.output: Likely issue: an app update changed expected field mappings. Recheck dropdown selections, add test records, and monitor failed runs.

best_practices: Use dropdown field selectors when platforms provide them instead of typing display text manually.
Add explicit error handling, duplicate checks, and notification steps for business-critical workflows.
Estimate task or operation volume before choosing between Zapier, Make, and custom code.
anti_patterns: Building long multi-app chains without monitoring, retries, or ownership for failed runs.
Hardcoding IDs, names, or routing values that should come from selected fields or lookup tables.
Keeping complex, high-volume workflows in no-code tools after platform limits become the main risk.

faq.question: What does this skill help me decide?
faq.answer: It helps decide whether Zapier, Make, or custom code fits a workflow based on complexity, reliability, and cost.

faq.question: Can it build a Zap or Make scenario for me?
faq.answer: It can draft the workflow design, but it does not create or deploy automations inside those platforms.

faq.question: Is it useful for existing automations?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review existing workflows for brittle field mappings, missing error paths, duplicates, and platform mismatch.

faq.question: Does it require technical knowledge?
faq.answer: No. Clear process details, app names, fields, and expected outcomes are usually enough to start.

faq.question: When should I use Make instead of Zapier?
faq.answer: Use Make when the workflow needs complex branching, data transformation, visual routing, or tighter operation cost control.

faq.question: When should I move from no-code to code?
faq.answer: Move to code when workflow volume, custom logic, reliability needs, or integration limits exceed no-code platform strengths.
